newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police say no evidence of racism in blaze.
newsitem.headline: German police say no evidence of racism in blaze.

text.p: German police said on Wednesday they have so far found no evidence there was a racist motive behind a blaze in which three Turks died in the western town of Krefeld on Monday.
"We are still investigating in all directions," a police spokesman said. "We still have not found any indications that there was a xenophobic motive."

Three members of a Turkish family died in the blaze, which investigators believe was set deliberately. Traces of flammable materials were found in front of a door as well as in an inside hallway, police said.
Authorities have offered a reward of 50,000 marks ($30,000) for information.

Members of the Turkish community laid flowers outside the apartment block and erected placards recalling a racist arson attack by four Germans in the town of Solingen in 1993 in which five members of a Turkish family died.

Turkey's Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, said on Tuesday Western education encouraged anti-Moslem feelings which led to racist attacks and said countries did not hand out adequate punishment for those guilty of such attacks.
Germany suffered a wave of racist violence following unification in 1990, particularly in the formerly communist east, and commentators fear economic problems are leading to a new surge of racism.

On Tuesday, a Turkish man was injured after a fire broke out at his home in the central German town of Haigerseelbach. Police said they had found a swastika Nazi symbol spray-painted on the back of the building.
Six members of a Turkish immigrant family died in the Netherlands last week in an arson attack being investigated amid suspicions that it may have been motivated by racial hatred.

German police in the eastern town of Dresden said arsonists had set fire to a children's recreation centre last month and drawn right-wing slogans and symbols on nearby buildings. Nobody was injured in the blaze. ($ = 1.670 German Marks)
